newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish truck chaos spreads nationwide.
newsitem.headline: Danish truck chaos spreads nationwide.

text.p: Danish lorry drivers blocking borders and sea-ports pledged on Tuesday to escalate their protest to the capital overnight, blocking roads into the city and causing commuter chaos on Wednesday morning.
"Police confirm the threat and advise motorists wishing to reach Copenhagen to consider using public transport," the national news agency Ritzau said.

Drivers have since Monday blocked goods traffic from crossing the land border with Germany and on Tuesday they broadened the blockade to most ports, halting exports to Norway and Sweden, radio and television reports said.
Traffic from the southern port of Esjberg to England was unaffected, independent TV2 television reported.
The protest, against government plans to cut drivers' overseas subsistence allowances, is unrelated to French drivers' nationwide roadblock protests.

Trapped at the Padborg crossing point on the Danish-German border were close to a million Christmas trees in danger of rotting, a spokesman for Denmark's Christmas Tree Growers' Association told Reuters.

"The blockade is nothing short of a catastrophe for our business just ahead of the festive season. We normally send 300 trucks full of Christmas trees and spruce to the south every day at this time of the year," a spokesman for Denmark's Christmas Tree Growers' Association told Reuters.

"Apart from the risk of fire, Christmas trees and spruce tightly packed into trucks rot away after a few days. We reckon that some 600 trucks carrying Christmas greenery have been stuck at the Danish-German border since the weekend," he said.
Each lorry carried an average of 1,500 trees, he added. They were among an estimated 1,500 Danish vehicles blocking the Padborg border to commercial traffic, private vehicles were allowed through.
Denmark is Europe's biggest exporter of Christmas trees, shipping six million trees and 25,000 tonnes of spruce each year and earning 500 million Danish crowns ($86 million).

Also at risk from the blockades were shipments of milk, cheese and meat, producers' organisations said. The Danish post office said that international mail and post between the Danish islands and the Jutland peninsula were subject to delays.
The government was scheduled to meet on Wednesday to consider the drivers' demands but Tax Minister Carsten Koch said his freedom to meet drivers' demands was limited.
"My responsibilty as a minister is to find a solution that will last and will not bring demands from other groups," he told TV2.
